messages:
Alex: Quick RFC follow-up — we keep getting billing mismatches for multi-stage inference flows (router -> cache -> model). Need a small design discussion on token-level cost attribution without pulling full traces through every layer.

Priya: Are we losing the billing context at the cache boundary today? I thought we propagated billing_key.

Marco: We do for most routable requests but not for cache hits from the KV layer. Cache returns precomputed tokens with no span/context.

Dana: This shows up especially with batching: a single GPU batch will include cached and non-cached requests; attribution logic needs to split GPU time across requests.

Yun: One immediate thought: emit a compact cost event at the point of token emission (including cache hits) rather than trying to stitch full spans later.

Alex: Proposal sketch: lightweight `cost_point` envelope emitted synchronously by the serving runtime whenever tokens are produced (or replayed from cache). Fields: `billing_key`, `model_version`, `token_count`, `gpu_ms`, `cache_hit` (bool), `batch_id` (optional), `tenant_id` (or tenant hash). This lets downstream aggregation compute per-tenant/per-model unit cost without carrying full trace payloads.

Marco: Example envelope (one-liner we can store as compact JSON):
```json
{"billing_key":"bk_abc123","tenant_hash":"t:42","model":"gptx-8b-q8","token_count":32,"gpu_ms":12.4,"cache_hit":true,"batch_id":"b-2026-04-01-7"}
```

Priya: Are we comfortable emitting billing_key-like tokens from caches? Storage/ingest cost goes up if we flood with these envelopes.

Marco: Mitigations: rate-limit emits per-request (emit summarized for long-lived streams), dedupe by `batch_id` for batched responses, and tiered retention (full raw for high-value tenants, daily rollups for others).

Dana: Implementation detail: runtime should reconstruct billing context at cache hit. Two options: 1) cache stores lightweight routing context with cached payload (increase cache entry size) or 2) runtime looks up last-seen mapping from incoming request headers (cheaper on cache but riskier for correctness).

Yun: Also need a privacy/compliance switch for Private deployments — hosted telemetry can't see raw billing_keys. We should support sending hashed keys or an on-prem telemetry connector that resolves and aggregates locally.

Alex: Performance SLO: adding `cost_point` emits should not add >1ms p99 to the request path. If sync emission costs too much, buffer and emit async with bounded delay (<=50ms) and attach `batch_id` to allow reconciliation.

Priya: Slight schema ask: include `model_quant_level` (quantization/precision) and `route_type` (primary/fallback) — helps cost-per-quality analysis.

Marco: Will include. Also propose a small helper function: merge batch-level GPU timings into per-request attribution using `batch_id` + `token_indexes` (we can infer token share).

Dana: Actionable plan: 
- Marco: write RFC w/ schema + retention tiers + example queries (due EOW).
- Dana: spike runtime prototype (branch: runtime/cost-point-proto) to emit envelope on cache and generation.
- Priya: run cost estimate for ingress + storage for 6-month window.
- Yun: design privacy mode + on-prem connector API.

Alex: Also: we need a fallback plan if `cost_point` emits get dropped — tie into existing APM traces as best-effort. We'll mark any missing attribution as `unknown_bucket` in billing reports.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: `cost-point-prototype` -> canary at 2026-04-01T04:00:00Z (ci: #4572) :rocket:

Priya: tiny nit — include `cache_layer_id` (edge vs global) so we can split edge-cache savings from central cache savings.

Marco: good call. adding `cache_layer_id` and `model_quant_level`. Also adding `emit_mode` = sync|async to help downstream correctness.

Alex: Cool. I'll cross-post summary to #eng-runtime and #product for visibility and ask SRE for monitoring on `cost_point.emit.latency` p50/p95/p99. @Dana @Marco please ping when RFC landed. :thumbsup:

Yun: One more edge case: multi-tenant batch co-location (different tenants in same GPU batch) — we must ensure batch reconciliation is deterministic. Add `tenant_shares` if we compute server-side.

Marco: noted. Will include the deterministic merge algorithm in the RFC (appendix).

Priya: Thanks — I'll start a rough cost projection table and share in the RFC thread.

Alex: Thanks everyone. Short sync if needed tomorrow 10am PT.
